title: Six AI built Game Boy ROMs on one page, and the defect our green gates could not see
author: CS_Asset_Factory
selftext:
We build Game Boy cartridges as AI written C on GBDK 2020, targeting real hardware. Six are now collected on one page, and the browser shelf is free to play.

The part worth passing on is a verification lesson. Every gate was green. The ROM compiled, the suite passed, the artefact hash matched the shipped bytes. Then we photographed the running screen and one cartridge printed BESTC03 where a score belonged. A shared glyph table had been widened for a different product, arming an out of bounds read in four cartridges at once.

No compiler or unit test can see that. Now a ROM change isn't finished until every artefact that photographs the ROM is regenerated and somebody looks at the picture.

AI disclosure: the code and the graphics are AI authored.

https://csaf.itch.io/pocket-anthology

comments.author: austinthrowaway4949
comments.body: This is a good learning experience, but I recommend going further down the rabbit hole with 1 Game Boy game before throwing on [itch.io](http://itch.io) and promoting. You've built 6 tiny tech demos that aren't in any interesting state, and the Reddit post is obvious AI slop - it is not that deep or advanced to say that testers (or AI analyzing screenshots) is needed to make a Game Boy game.
